questions.question: Market control under Alauddin Khilji aimed mainly to ________.

options.text: check price inflation for army provisions

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**check price inflation for army provisions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khilji** (reigned 1296–1316) was a prominent Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate, known for his military campaigns and administrative reforms.
 
• One of his major administrative measures was the regulation of the market to control prices, with the primary aim of ensuring the supply of provisions for his large standing army at reasonable rates.
 
• He established a **centralized market control mechanism** that included strict price regulations for essential commodities such as grains, clothes, and other goods required for the army.
 
• Alauddin Khilji ensured strict implementation of these price controls by appointing market inspectors (**Shahna-i-Mandi**) who were responsible for monitoring the markets and preventing hoarding or price manipulation.
 
• This system helped in maintaining a steady supply of provisions for his army and preventing inflation during wartime campaigns, which was crucial for his military success and stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Market Control Policy:**

 
 
• The primary purpose of the market control was to **stabilize prices** and ensure the availability of essential commodities for the army.
 
• This policy was not aimed at encouraging luxury goods or foreign trade but was meant to support the Sultanate's military and administrative machinery.
 
 
 
• **Implementation Measures:**
 
 
• Alauddin Khilji introduced a system of **price lists** for all commodities, including grains, textiles, and cattle.
 
• He established government-run granaries to ensure a steady supply of grains, which was critical during famines or shortages.
 
• The state directly intervened in trade and ensured that merchants adhered to fixed prices under strict penalties.
 
 
 
• **Market Supervision:**
 
 
• A special officer, the **Shahna-i-Mandi**, was appointed to oversee the markets and ensure compliance with price regulations.
 
• Hoarding and black-market trading were severely punished to prevent artificial price hikes.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Policy:**
 
 
• The market control policy helped in maintaining the **economic stability** of the Sultanate and supported the Sultan's ambitious military campaigns.
 
• It also helped in protecting the common people from price exploitation by traders during periods of scarcity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of Alauddin Khilji:**

 
 
• Alauddin Khilji’s market reforms were part of his broader administrative and military strategies.
 
• He was one of the first rulers to establish a permanent standing army, and the market control system was designed to support this major military innovation.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Rulers:**
 
 
• Unlike other rulers who focused on luxury goods or foreign trade, Alauddin’s reforms were practical and aimed at military efficiency.
 
• His market control policy set a precedent for later rulers in terms of state intervention in the economy.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Milkha Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Milkha Singh**, popularly known as the "Flying Sikh," was the first Indian to win a **gold medal** at the **Commonwealth Games**.
 
• He achieved this milestone in the year **1958** during the Commonwealth Games held in **Cardiff, Wales**.
 
• Milkha Singh competed in the **440 yards race** and secured the gold medal, making history for Indian athletics on an international platform.
 
• His victory was considered a breakthrough moment for Indian sports, as he was competing against some of the best athletes in the world at the time.
 
• Milkha Singh's achievement inspired generations of Indian athletes and showcased the potential of Indian sports on the global stage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh:**

 
 
• Born on **20 November 1929** in **Govindpura, Punjab (now in Pakistan)**.
 
• He represented India in three Olympics: **1956**, **1960**, and **1964**.
 
• Milkha Singh narrowly missed a medal in the **1960 Rome Olympics**, finishing fourth in the **400 meters** race.
 
• He was awarded the **Padma Shri**, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in recognition of his contributions to sports.
 
 
 
• **Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• The Commonwealth Games are a multi-sport event involving athletes from the **Commonwealth of Nations**.
 
• India has been participating in the Commonwealth Games since **1934**.
 
• Milkha Singh's gold medal in **1958** was India's first-ever gold medal at these Games.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Achievements at the Commonwealth Games:**
 
 
• India has won numerous medals since Milkha Singh's historic win, with athletes excelling in sports like **boxing, wrestling, badminton, and shooting**.
 
• Notable names include **PV Sindhu** in badminton, **Vijender Singh** in boxing, and **Saina Nehwal** in badminton.
 
 
 
• **Legacy of Milkha Singh:**
 
 
• Milkha Singh's story has inspired countless athletes, and his life was depicted in the popular Bollywood movie **"Bhaag Milkha Bhaag"** (2013).
 
• He passed away on **18 June 2021** at the age of **91** due to complications from COVID-19.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Milkha Singh's Contribution to Indian Sports:**

 
 
• Milkha Singh remains one of the most iconic figures in Indian sports history.
 
• He helped elevate the status of athletics in India, inspiring investment and recognition for the sport.
 
• His determination and perseverance serve as a model for aspiring athletes.
 
 
 
• **India's Progress in Athletics:**
 
 
• Following Milkha Singh's lead, India has seen significant growth in track and field events.
 
• Notable athletes like **PT Usha**, **Neeraj Chopra**, and **Anju Bobby George** have brought further glory to Indian athletics.
 
• Neeraj Chopra's gold medal win in javelin at the **2020 Tokyo Olympics** was a landmark achievement in Indian sports.

questions.question: Which of the following is a distinctive feature of tribal settlements in India?

options.text: Scattered or linear village pattern in forested or hilly areas

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Scattered or linear village pattern in forested or hilly areas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tribal settlements in India** are typically characterized by a **scattered or linear village pattern**, especially in forested or hilly areas. This pattern arises due to the geographical terrain, economic activities, and cultural practices of tribal communities.
 
• Tribal communities often live in **remote and inaccessible locations**, including hills, forests, and mountainous regions, which makes scattered settlements more practical and sustainable.
 
• These settlements are designed to ensure proximity to natural resources such as forests, water bodies, and agricultural land, which are vital for their livelihood. Tribal communities predominantly engage in activities such as **subsistence agriculture, hunting, gathering, and fishing**.
 
• Unlike urban areas, tribal settlements do not have **planned city layouts** or modern infrastructure. Their houses are typically built using locally available materials such as bamboo, wood, and mud, reflecting their deep connection to nature.
 
• Tribal settlements are often characterized by a sense of community living and shared resources. These settlements foster a strong **social and cultural bond** among tribal members, which is a distinctive aspect of their lifestyle.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Option 1: Modern infrastructure and transportation**

 
 
• This is not a characteristic of tribal settlements as they are located in remote areas with limited access to modern amenities and transportation systems.
 
• Such infrastructure is more common in urban and semi-urban areas, not in tribal regions.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: Skyscrapers**
 
 
• Skyscrapers are a feature of urban environments and metropolitan cities. They are built using advanced technology and are designed for economic or residential purposes.
 
• Tribal settlements typically consist of small, simple houses made from natural materials, and skyscrapers are not part of their settlement pattern.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: Planned city layouts**
 
 
• Planned city layouts are found in urban and metropolitan areas where settlements are organized systematically with infrastructure like roads, drainage systems, and zoning.
 
• Tribal settlements are generally unplanned and evolve organically based on the geographical and environmental conditions.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Scattered or linear village pattern in forested or hilly areas**
 
 
• This is the correct answer and a distinctive feature of tribal settlements. The geographical terrain and the dependence on natural resources shape the scattered and linear patterns of these settlements.
 
• Examples include tribal settlements in states like **Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and northeastern states** of India, which are primarily located in forested and hilly regions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal settlements:**

 
 
• They represent the **original inhabitants** of India and are spread across various states.
 
• India has a significant tribal population, constituting about **8.6% of the total population** as per the **2011 Census**.
 
• Tribal communities are recognized under the **Fifth and Sixth Schedule** of the Indian Constitution, ensuring their rights and protection.
 
 
 
• **Forest Rights Act, 2006:**
 
 
• The act recognizes the rights of forest-dwelling tribal communities to access and manage the forest resources on which they depend.
 
• It aims to empower tribal communities and ensure their participation in forest conservation.

questions.question: Who has the power to give directions to the State Government to ensure compliance with Union laws?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 256** of the **Indian Constitution** empowers the **President of India** to ensure that the State Governments comply with the laws made by the Parliament and any existing laws that apply to that State.
 
• The President can issue **directions to the State Government** if it fails to comply with the legislative requirements.
 
• The power of issuing directions is not vested in any other institution such as the **Prime Minister, Parliament, or Supreme Court.**
 
• The provision ensures the **federal structure** of governance in India, where the Union Government can guide the States in implementing laws uniformly across the country.
 
• If a State Government fails to comply with these directions, the President is empowered to take necessary actions, which may include invoking **Article 356** and imposing President’s Rule in that State.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 256 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It states that the executive power of every State shall be so exercised as to ensure compliance with the laws made by Parliament and any existing laws applicable in that State.
 
• The Union Government can issue directions to a State as it deems necessary for this purpose.
 
 
 
• **Article 356:**
 
 
• If a State Government fails to comply with the directions issued under Article 256, the President can invoke Article 356.
 
• Article 356 allows the imposition of **President’s Rule** in the State, effectively bringing the State under the control of the Union Government temporarily.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President:**
 
 
• The President acts as the Constitutional Head of India and exercises powers as defined under the Constitution.
 
• The President’s authority in ensuring compliance with Union laws is an example of the checks and balances in the Indian federal system.
 
 
 
• **Difference from Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The **Supreme Court** ensures the judicial review of laws and resolves disputes between the Union and States. However, it does not have the power to issue directions to the State Governments for compliance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prime Minister of India:**

 
 
• The Prime Minister is the head of the government and advises the President but does not have the constitutional authority to issue directions to State Governments for compliance with Union laws.
 
 
 
• **Parliament of India:**
 
 
• The Parliament makes laws but does not execute or enforce them. The responsibility of ensuring compliance lies with the executive branch.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India:**
 
 
• It ensures the interpretation of laws and resolves disputes but does not issue directions to States for compliance with Union laws.
 
 
 
• **Role of the President:**
 
 
• The President acts on the advice of the Union Council of Ministers, led by the Prime Minister, but is the constitutional authority for issuing directions under Article 256.

questions.question: In June 2025, a 'Maha Kumbhabhishekam' was performed after 270 years at the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple, located in which Indian State?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple** is located in **Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala**. It is one of the most famous temples in India and is renowned for its opulence and historical significance.
 
• The **Maha Kumbhabhishekam** is a grand ritual performed in Hindu temples, involving the sanctification of deities and the temple. In June 2025, this ritual was conducted at the Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple after **270 years**, making it a historic event.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Lord Vishnu** and is one of the 108 Divya Desams (sacred places of worship for Vaishnavites).
 
• The architectural style of the temple is a blend of **Kerala and Dravidian architecture**, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the region.
 
• The temple is well-known for its immense treasures discovered in its underground vaults, which include gold, jewels, and other valuables, making it one of the richest temples in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple:**

 
 
• The temple is mentioned in historical records dating back to the 6th century AD and has been a significant pilgrimage site for centuries.
 
• The presiding deity, **Lord Padmanabha**, is depicted in a reclining posture on the serpent Anantha (Adi Shesha).
 
• The temple is managed by the royal family of Travancore, and it is deeply connected to the history and traditions of Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Maha Kumbhabhishekam:**
 
 
• This sacred ceremony is performed to rejuvenate the divine energy of the temple and its deities.
 
• The process involves elaborate rituals, including chanting of Vedic hymns, homas (fire sacrifices), and the pouring of sanctified water on the temple and its deities.
 
• This ritual is typically conducted once every 12 years or longer, depending on the temple's tradition.
 
 
 
• **Kerala's Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Kerala is known as “**God’s Own Country**” due to its natural beauty, cultural heritage, and religious significance.
 
• The state is home to numerous ancient temples, each with its unique history, architecture, and traditions.
 
• Kerala's festivals, such as **Onam** and **Vishu**, play a significant role in its cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Other Famous Temples in Kerala:**
 
 
• **Guruvayur Temple**: Known as the Dwarka of the South and dedicated to Lord Krishna.
 
• **Sabarimala Temple**: Dedicated to Lord Ayyappa, it attracts millions of devotees annually.
 
• **Chottanikkara Temple**: Famous for its deity Bhagavathy, considered a form of Goddess Lakshmi.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The 2025 Maha Kumbhabhishekam marked the first such event at the temple in **270 years**, underlining its rarity and importance in maintaining the temple's sanctity.
 
• **Security and Treasure:** The temple gained international attention after the discovery of its underground vaults containing treasures worth billions of dollars. These treasures are believed to have been offerings from devotees over centuries.
 
• **Tourism:** The Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple is a major tourist attraction in Kerala, drawing devotees, historians, and tourists from around the globe.
 
• **Dress Code:** The temple enforces a traditional dress code for visitors, emphasizing its commitment to preserving ancient customs.

questions.question: The 44th Amendment (1978) removed which of the following from the list of Fundamental Rights, converting it into a mere legal right under Article 300A?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Right to Property**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **44th Amendment Act of 1978** of the Indian Constitution removed the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a mere legal right under **Article 300A**.
 
• The **Right to Property** was originally a Fundamental Right under **Article 31** of the Constitution.
 
• The amendment ensured that the Right to Property was no longer a guaranteed Fundamental Right but rather a constitutional right. This change was made to prevent misuse of the right to property against the state’s authority to enforce land reforms.
 
• Under **Article 300A**, no person can be deprived of their property except by the authority of law. This means that the state can acquire private property for public purposes but only with proper legal procedures.
 
• The removal of the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right was aimed at balancing individual rights with socio-economic justice and facilitating equitable land redistribution.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• The Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution and are considered essential for the holistic development of individuals.
 
• These rights include **Right to Equality** (Articles 14-18), **Right to Freedom** (Articles 19-22), **Right to Constitutional Remedies** (Article 32), and others.
 
 
 
• **Right to Property:**
 
 
• Initially, the Right to Property was a part of Fundamental Rights under Articles 19(1)(f) and 31.
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** first diluted the Right to Property, and the **44th Amendment Act of 1978** finally removed it as a Fundamental Right.
 
 
 
• **Article 300A:**
 
 
• Introduced by the 44th Amendment Act, it states that no person shall be deprived of their property except by the authority of law.
 
• It provides legal protection to property rights but does not guarantee these rights as Fundamental Rights.
 
 
 
• **Land Reforms:**
 
 
• Land reforms were crucial in redistributing land to ensure social and economic equity.
 
• The removal of the Right to Property as a Fundamental Right allowed the government to implement land reforms more effectively without judicial interference.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Other Fundamental Rights:**

 
 
• **Right to Equality:** Ensures equal treatment before the law and prohibits discrimination based on caste, religion, gender, etc.
 
• **Right to Constitutional Remedies:** Allows individuals to approach the courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights.
 
• **Right to Education:** Guaranteed under Article 21A, it provides free and compulsory education to children aged 6-14 years.
 
 
 
• **Global Context:**
 
 
• In many countries, property rights are safeguarded as legal or constitutional rights and not as fundamental rights.
 
• The change in India aligns with global practices, allowing governments to balance individual property rights with societal needs.

questions.question: Which of the following subjects was moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment Act?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act of 1976** was one of the most comprehensive amendments to the **Indian Constitution**. It brought about significant changes to the division of powers between the **Union and State governments**.
 
• One of the major changes introduced by the 42nd Amendment was the transfer of the subject of **Education** from the **State List** to the **Concurrent List**. This allowed both the Union and State governments to legislate on matters related to education.
 
• The amendment was aimed at ensuring a more uniform educational policy across the country and addressing the growing importance of education in national development.
 
• This move was significant because the Concurrent List subjects empower both the central and state governments to legislate, ensuring better collaboration in policymaking and implementation of educational reforms.
 
• Other subjects such as **Forests**, **Wildlife Protection**, and **Weighs & Measures** were also shifted to the Concurrent List through the 42nd Amendment Act, showcasing the importance of unified governance in these critical areas.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Education.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **State List:**

 
 
• The **State List** comprises subjects on which only the state legislatures can legislate, as per the **Seventh Schedule** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Examples of subjects in the State List include **Police**, **Agriculture**, and **Public Health**.
 
• Before the 42nd Amendment, **Education** was exclusively under the purview of the states.
 
 
 
• **Concurrent List:**
 
 
• The **Concurrent List** contains subjects where both the Union and State governments have the authority to legislate.
 
• Examples of subjects in the Concurrent List include **Education**, **Forests**, **Trade Unions**, and **Marriage**.
 
• If there is a conflict between Union and State laws on a Concurrent List subject, the law enacted by the Union government prevails.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**
 
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act** was enacted in **1976** during the Emergency under the leadership of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**.
 
• It is often referred to as the "Mini Constitution" due to the extensive changes it brought to the Indian Constitution.
 
• In addition to moving subjects to the Concurrent List, the amendment introduced changes to the Preamble, Directive Principles of State Policy, and the relationship between the Union and States.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Education:**
 
 
• **Education** is a critical tool for socio-economic development, and its inclusion in the Concurrent List reflects the emphasis on creating a unified and national approach to educational policies.
 
• This change enabled the Union government to launch nationwide educational programs like the **National Policy on Education** and schemes such as the **Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan**.
 
• It also facilitates better coordination between states and the center in implementing large-scale reforms in education.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seventh Schedule:** The Indian Constitution divides subjects into three lists: Union List, State List, and Concurrent List under the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• **Union List:** Contains subjects exclusively under the Union government's jurisdiction, such as **Defense**, **Foreign Affairs**, and **Atomic Energy**.
 
• **Federal Structure:** The division of powers between the Union and States ensures a balance of governance, but the Concurrent List allows cooperation on critical subjects like education.
 
• **Role of Education:** Moving education to the Concurrent List reflects its importance in achieving national goals like **universal literacy**, **skill development**, and **human capital enhancement**.

questions.question: What does the abbreviation ASCII stand for?

options.text: Automated System for Computer Integrated Information

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**American Standard Code for Information Interchange**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **American Standard Code for Information Interchange (ASCII)** is a character encoding standard used for electronic communication.
 
• It was developed in **1963** by the American National Standards Institute (**ANSI**) to standardize the representation of text in computers and electronic devices.
 
• ASCII uses **7-bit binary numbers** to represent **128 unique characters**, including English letters (uppercase and lowercase), digits (0–9), punctuation marks, and control characters.
 
• This encoding method ensures compatibility across different devices and platforms, making it a fundamental standard in computing systems.
 
• ASCII is widely used in programming, data storage, and communication protocols due to its simplicity and efficiency.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development and History:**

 
 
• The ASCII standard was first published in **1963** and underwent updates in **1967** to include additional characters.
 
• It was originally designed for **telecommunication systems** and is now extensively utilized in computer systems worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Structure of ASCII:**
 
 
• ASCII comprises **control characters** (0–31 and 127) and **printable characters** (32–126).
 
• Control characters include instructions like **line feed** (LF) and **carriage return** (CR).
 
• Printable characters include **letters, digits, and symbols**, such as **A, 1, !**, and **@**.
 
 
 
• **Extended ASCII:**
 
 
• Extended ASCII uses **8 bits** to represent **256 characters**, adding support for graphical symbols and international characters.
 
• It is commonly used in applications requiring a broader range of characters, such as European languages.
 
 
 
• **Applications of ASCII:**
 
 
• ASCII is used in **text files, programming languages**, and **communication protocols** like HTTP and FTP.
 
• It serves as the foundation for other encoding standards, such as **UTF-8**, which supports a wider range of characters.
 
• ASCII codes are critical for ensuring compatibility between different systems and devices.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Standards:**
 
 
• Unlike ASCII, **Unicode** provides encoding for thousands of characters across multiple languages.
 
• Unicode standards like **UTF-8** are backward-compatible with ASCII and widely adopted for global applications.

• Space agencies like **NASA** and **Roscosmos** have used similar technologies in their launch vehicles, providing a proven track record for semicryogenic engines.
 
• India’s development of this technology will enhance its position in the **global space industry**, promoting self-reliance and competitiveness.

• **Cost-Effectiveness:**
 
 
• Using kerosene as fuel is more economical and environmentally friendly compared to traditional cryogenic fuels.

• Developing indigenous propulsion systems like the semicryogenic engine will reduce India’s dependency on foreign technology and enhance national security.

questions.question: As per the 2025 Human Development Index (HDI) report, what is India's HDI value for 2023 that places it in the medium human development category?

__
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):** The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index published annually by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)**. It measures the social and economic development of countries based on three major dimensions: **health, education,** and **standard of living**.
 
• **India's HDI Value:** As per the **2025 Human Development Index report**, India's HDI value for **2023** is **0.685**, which positions the country in the **medium human development category**.
 
• **Global Ranking:** India's HDI value places it among countries striving to achieve significant progress in human development. It shows **improvements in life expectancy, education levels, and income per capita**.
 
• **Medium Human Development Category:** Countries with HDI values between **0.55** and **0.7** are classified under the medium human development category. India's position reflects the **ongoing efforts to balance economic growth and social development**.
 
• **Development Challenges:** Despite improvements, India still faces challenges in areas such as **reducing inequality, improving healthcare infrastructure, and enhancing education quality**, which are critical to achieving higher HDI rankings in the future.

• **UNDP and HDI:**

• **Article 243D** of the **Indian Constitution** deals with the **reservation of seats** in every Panchayat for Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women.

__

• It is a **three-tier system** of governance at the village, intermediate, and district levels, as introduced by the **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992**.
 
• The Act added **Part IX** to the Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," which includes Articles **243** to **243O**.
 
• The system aims to ensure **local self-governance** in rural areas, empowering local communities to participate in decision-making processes.

• **Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes:**

• Reservation in Panchayats aims to empower these communities by providing them with a platform to participate in local governance and decision-making processes.
 
 
 
• **State Election Commission:**

• **Significance of Article 243D:**

 
 
• It ensures the **political empowerment** of marginalized communities and women at the grassroots level.

• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act:**

questions.question: Who is considered unemployed under the Usual Status (US) measure?

options.text: Someone working only one day a week
Someone not working but seeking work over a long period

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Someone not working but seeking work over a long period**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Usual Status (US) measure** of unemployment refers to a person being unemployed if they have been seeking work but have not been able to find employment for a substantial or prolonged period.
 
• This measure focuses on individuals who are actively seeking work and are available for work but are unable to secure employment due to various factors such as lack of opportunities or skills mismatch.
 
• Under the **Usual Status definition**, unemployment is assessed over a longer reference period, typically one year, compared to other measures of unemployment that might use shorter timeframes such as a week or month.
 
• Unlike temporary unemployment or underemployment (e.g., working part-time or occasionally), the US measure prioritizes those who are persistently unemployed and seeking work, hence offering insights into chronic unemployment in the economy.
 
• The measure is widely used in surveys conducted by organizations like the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)** in India to gauge unemployment trends over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Different measures of unemployment:**

 
 
• **Usual Status (US) measure:** Assesses unemployment over a reference period of one year, focusing on individuals who are persistently unemployed.
 
• **Current Weekly Status (CWS) measure:** Evaluates unemployment based on the number of days a person was employed or unemployed during the reference week.
 
• **Current Daily Status (CDS) measure:** Considers unemployment on a daily basis, offering a more granular view of employment trends.
 
 
 
• **Key differences between employed and unemployed:**
 
 
• **Employed:** Individuals who are engaged in economic activities and earning wages or profits.
 
• **Unemployed:** Individuals who are not engaged in economic activities but are actively seeking work and are available to work.
 
• **Underemployed:** Individuals who are working but not to their full potential or capacity, such as part-time workers wanting full-time jobs.
 
 
 
• **Relevance of unemployment data:**
 
 
• Helps policymakers understand the health of the economy and assess the need for employment generation programs.
 
• Important for addressing social welfare concerns and ensuring economic stability.
 
• Provides insights into the effectiveness of skill development initiatives and educational policies.
 
 
 
• **Examples of chronic unemployment:**
 
 
• Individuals lacking skills relevant to modern industries (e.g., due to technological changes).
 
• People residing in regions with limited economic opportunities, such as rural areas or regions with low industrialization.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option Analysis:**

 
 
• **Someone working only one day a week:** This describes **underemployment**, not unemployment. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
• **Someone retired from work:** Retired individuals are not considered part of the labor force, as they are not seeking work. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
• **Someone not working but seeking work over a long period:** This fits the definition of unemployment under the Usual Status measure. Hence, this statement is correct.
 
• **Someone working part-time:** Part-time workers are considered employed, even if they work fewer hours than desired. Hence, this statement is incorrect.
 
 
 
• The **Usual Status measure** is widely used in India as it reflects long-term unemployment trends, unlike the CWS and CDS measures which are more suited for assessing short-term unemployment.
 
• According to the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** conducted by the NSSO, the unemployment rate under the Usual Status provides a comprehensive view of structural unemployment and is considered a critical indicator for policy-making.

questions.question: What is the value of one curie (Ci) in SI units of radioactivity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3.7×10¹⁰ disintegrations per second**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **curie (Ci)** is a non-SI unit of radioactivity that is widely used in nuclear science and engineering.
 
• One curie is defined as the activity of a radioactive substance that undergoes **3.7×10¹⁰ disintegrations per second**.
 
• This value was based on the approximate activity of 1 gram of radium-226, a radioactive isotope discovered by **Marie Curie and Pierre Curie**.
 
• The curie is commonly used to describe the intensity of radiation sources in various applications, including medical, industrial, and scientific fields.
 
• The SI unit of radioactivity is the **becquerel (Bq)**, which corresponds to one disintegration per second. Hence, 1 curie equals **3.7×10¹⁰ becquerels**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Marie Curie's Contribution:**

 
 
• Marie Curie and Pierre Curie discovered **radium** and **polonium**, leading to the concept of radioactivity.
 
• The unit "curie" was named in honor of their groundbreaking work in the field of radioactive decay.
 
 
 
• **Radioactivity Measurement Units:**
 
 
• The **becquerel (Bq)** is the SI unit of radioactivity, representing one disintegration per second.
 
• Other units like the **gray (Gy)** and **sievert (Sv)** measure absorbed radiation dose and biological effects, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Curie:**
 
 
• The curie is used in industries such as **nuclear medicine**, **radiography**, and **research**.
 
• It helps quantify the activity of radioactive isotopes used for diagnostic imaging and cancer treatment.
 
 
 
• **Conversion to SI Units:**
 
 
• 1 curie = **3.7×10¹⁰ becquerels**, making it a convenient unit for large-scale radioactive sources.
 
• In scientific studies, the use of becquerel is preferred for precision and adherence to SI norms.

questions.question: What happens to tectonic plates at divergent boundaries?

options.text: They move away from each other.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They move away from each other.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Divergent boundaries** occur when **tectonic plates move away from each other**. This movement creates space for magma to rise from the mantle, forming new crust. 
 
• This process commonly occurs at **mid-ocean ridges**, where the oceanic crust is generated, such as the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge**.
 
• At divergent boundaries, the **upwelling magma solidifies**, creating features like rift valleys and underwater volcanic ridges.
 
• The movement of plates at divergent boundaries is a key part of the **tectonic cycle**, contributing to the recycling of the Earth’s crust. 
 
• Divergent boundaries are associated with geological phenomena such as **earthquakes** and **volcanic activity**, but these tend to be less intense compared to convergent boundaries. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Plate Tectonics:**

 
 
• The theory of **plate tectonics** explains the movement of Earth’s lithospheric plates over the asthenosphere.
 
• There are three types of plate boundaries: **divergent, convergent, and transform boundaries**.
 
• These movements are driven by forces such as **mantle convection**, ridge-push, and slab-pull mechanisms. 
 
 
 
• **Mid-Ocean Ridges:**
 
 
• Mid-ocean ridges are underwater mountain systems formed by plate tectonics at divergent boundaries. 
 
• They are the site of **seafloor spreading**, where new oceanic crust is created as magma rises and solidifies.
 
• Examples include the **Mid-Atlantic Ridge** and the **East Pacific Rise**.
 
 
 
• **Rift Valleys:**
 
 
• In continental regions, divergent boundaries can form **rift valleys**, which are elongated troughs with steep walls. 
 
• An example is the **Great Rift Valley** in East Africa, which is caused by the splitting of the African Plate.
 
 
 
• **Associated Earthquakes:**
 
 
• Earthquakes at divergent boundaries are generally less intense compared to those at convergent boundaries.
 
• These earthquakes occur due to the **stretching and fracturing** of the Earth's crust as plates move apart.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic Activity:**
 
 
• Volcanic activity at divergent boundaries occurs due to the upwelling of magma. 
 
• This contributes to the formation of volcanic islands and ridges such as **Iceland**, which lies on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1 - They stay in one place:** This is incorrect as tectonic plates are in constant motion due to mantle convection forces.
 
• **Option 3 - They slide past one another:** This refers to **transform boundaries**, not divergent boundaries. Examples include the **San Andreas Fault**.
 
• **Option 4 - They move towards each other:** This describes **convergent boundaries**, where plates collide, leading to features like mountains and subduction zones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **gomat** in the **Rigveda** refers to someone who possesses cows, which were considered a symbol of wealth and prosperity in ancient Vedic society.
 
• The Rigvedic society was agrarian, and cows were highly valued for their milk, dung (used as fuel and manure), and as an economic asset. Hence, a person with many cows was considered wealthy.
 
• The term "gomat" is derived from the Sanskrit word "go," meaning cow, and "mat," meaning possession or having.
 
• In the Rigvedic hymns, wealth was often measured in terms of cattle rather than gold or money, making the term synonymous with a wealthy person.
 
• Cows were associated with abundance, nourishment, and social status, and thus, individuals described as "gomat" held an esteemed position in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Rigveda:**

 
 
• The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas, composed around **1500 BCE** in ancient India.
 
• It consists of **10 mandalas (books)** and contains **1028 hymns** dedicated to various deities such as Indra, Agni, Varuna, and Soma.
 
• The Rigvedic society was primarily agrarian, and cattle, especially cows, were considered the backbone of the economy.
 
• It provides insights into the early Indo-Aryan civilization, their beliefs, culture, and socio-economic practices.
 
 
 
• **The importance of cows in Vedic society:**
 
 
• Cows were regarded as sacred and were often offered in sacrifices during religious ceremonies.
 
• The possession of cows was a sign of wealth, and they were used in trade and as gifts during important events.
 
• The cow's utility extended beyond milk to dung, which was used as manure and fuel, making it vital for agriculture and daily life.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly represents the function of dietary fibre in the human diet?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aids Digestion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dietary fibre**, also known as roughage or bulk, is primarily found in plant-based foods such as fruits, vegetables, whole grains, nuts, and seeds.
 
• It is a type of carbohydrate that is not digestible by human enzymes, meaning it passes through the digestive system relatively intact.
 
• One of the primary functions of dietary fibre is to **aid digestion** by adding bulk to the stool, which helps prevent constipation and promotes regular bowel movements.
 
• Dietary fibre can help maintain a healthy gut microbiome by serving as food for beneficial gut bacteria, which produce short-chain fatty acids that contribute to gut health.
 
• Soluble fibre can help regulate blood sugar levels and lower cholesterol by slowing the absorption of sugar and binding to cholesterol in the digestive tract, though these benefits are secondary to its primary role in digestion.
 
• It does not provide energy directly, as it is not broken down into glucose, nor does it contribute to muscle building or increase cholesterol levels.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Dietary Fibre:**

 
 
• **Soluble fibre:** Found in foods like oats, barley, and fruits such as apples and citrus. It dissolves in water and forms a gel-like substance that can help lower cholesterol and stabilize blood sugar levels.
 
• **Insoluble fibre:** Found in foods like whole grains, nuts, seeds, and vegetables. It does not dissolve in water and primarily adds bulk to stool, aiding in regular bowel movements and preventing constipation.
 
 
 
• **Health Benefits:**
 
 
• Consuming adequate dietary fibre can help prevent several digestive disorders such as **diverticular disease**, **irritable bowel syndrome** (IBS), and **constipation**.
 
• Dietary fibre is associated with a lower risk of chronic diseases such as **type 2 diabetes**, **heart disease**, and **certain types of cancer**, particularly colorectal cancer.
 
• It can contribute to weight management by promoting a feeling of fullness, thereby reducing overall calorie intake.
 
 
 
• **Recommended Intake:**
 
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** recommends adults consume at least **25-30 grams** of dietary fibre daily from a variety of food sources.
 
• Children and adolescents require slightly less depending on their age, ranging from **15-25 grams per day**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of High-Fibre Foods:**
 
 
• Whole grains like **brown rice**, **quinoa**, and **whole wheat bread**.
 
• Legumes such as **lentils**, **chickpeas**, and **black beans**.
 
• Fruits such as **bananas**, **apples**, and **berries**.
 
• Vegetables like **broccoli**, **carrots**, and **spinach**.
 
• Nuts and seeds such as **almonds**, **chia seeds**, and **flaxseeds**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Misconceptions about Dietary Fibre:**

 
 
• Dietary fibre does not directly provide **energy** or **calories** because it is not digestible.
 
• It does not help build **muscle**, as its function is primarily related to digestion and gut health.
 
• While dietary fibre can lower **cholesterol**, it does not increase it.
 
 
 
• **Global Trends:**
 
 
• Many regions, including **North America** and **Europe**, report a significant fibre deficiency in their diets, often due to the prevalence of processed foods.
 
• Countries such as **India** and **China**, with diets rich in grains, legumes, and vegetables, typically meet or exceed recommended fibre levels.
 
 
 
• **Practical Tips for Increasing Fibre Intake:**
 
 
• Replace refined grains with **whole grains**, such as switching from white bread to whole wheat bread.
 
• Add more **fruits** and **vegetables** to meals and snacks.
 
• Incorporate **nuts**, **seeds**, and **legumes** into daily meals.
 
• Hydrate adequately, as fibre requires water to move effectively through the digestive system.

questions.solution:

__
 
• **Human Papillomavirus (HPV) test** is primarily used for the diagnosis of **cervical cancer**, caused by persistent infection with high-risk HPV types.
 
• India introduced two indigenous HPV testing kits in **April 2025** to provide accessible and affordable diagnostic solutions for cervical cancer detection.
 
• **Cervical cancer** is the **second-most common cancer** among women in India, particularly affecting women in the age group of **30-60 years**.
 
• HPV testing is a **screening method** used to detect high-risk types of HPV that might lead to cervical cancer. It is more effective than the traditional Pap smear test.
 
• Regular screening, vaccination against HPV, and early detection through such kits can significantly reduce the **mortality rate** caused by cervical cancer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Human Papillomavirus (HPV):**

 
 
• HPV is a group of viruses, with more than **100 types**, of which around 14 types are high-risk and associated with cancer.
 
• It is the most common viral infection of the reproductive tract and is transmitted through sexual contact.
 
• The virus can cause abnormal changes in the cells of the cervix, which may lead to cancer if left untreated.
 
• HPV vaccines, such as **Gardasil** and **Cervarix**, are effective in preventing infections caused by high-risk HPV types.
 
 
 
• **Cervical Cancer:**
 
 
• Cervical cancer is caused by the uncontrolled growth of cells in the cervix, the lower part of the uterus connecting to the vagina.
 
• Symptoms may include **abnormal vaginal bleeding**, pelvic pain, and pain during intercourse.
 
• It can be prevented through **vaccination**, regular screening (Pap smear and HPV test), and early detection.
 
• Globally, cervical cancer accounts for approximately **604,000 new cases** and **342,000 deaths** annually (WHO data).
 
 
 
• **Other Cancer Types:**
 
 
• **Brain Cancer:** A rare cancer that affects the brain's tissues. It has no connection to HPV infection.
 
• **Prostate Cancer:** This affects the prostate gland in men and is unrelated to HPV.
 
• **Blood Cancer:** Includes leukemia, lymphoma, and myeloma, none of which are linked to HPV.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Indigenous HPV Testing Kits:**
 
 
• Indigenous kits help reduce the **cost of diagnosis** and make cervical cancer screening accessible to women in rural and low-income areas.
 
• Promoting such kits aligns with India's efforts to achieve **universal health coverage** and reduce the burden of preventable diseases.
 
• It also enhances India's capabilities in biotechnology and medical diagnostics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **HPV Vaccination:**

 
 
• HPV vaccines are recommended for girls aged **9-14 years** for maximum efficacy.
 
• India launched its first indigenously developed HPV vaccine, **CERVAVAC**, in **2023**.
 
 
 
• **Global Efforts to Eliminate Cervical Cancer:**
 
 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** has set a target to eliminate cervical cancer as a public health problem by achieving **90% vaccination coverage**, 70% screening, and 90% treatment by 2030.
 
• Cervical cancer is highly preventable and treatable if detected early, making such initiatives critical.

The correct answer is __**Dmitri Mendeleev**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**, a Russian chemist, is credited with publishing the first widely recognized version of the **periodic table** in **1869**.
 
• He arranged the elements in order of increasing **atomic mass** and grouped them based on their chemical properties.
 
• Mendeleev left gaps in his table for elements that were not yet discovered and even predicted their properties, which was later confirmed by discoveries like **gallium** and **germanium**.
 
• The periodic table proposed by Mendeleev helped in understanding the **periodic trends** and relationships between elements, revolutionizing the study of chemistry.
 
• Mendeleev's periodic table provided a systematic framework for organizing elements, making it possible to predict the existence and properties of unknown elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **John Alexander Newlands:**

 
 
• Newlands proposed the **Law of Octaves** in **1864**, suggesting that every eighth element has similar properties when arranged by atomic weight.
 
• However, his classification was limited to known elements at the time and did not account for undiscovered elements, leading to inconsistencies.
 
 
 
• **Johann Dobereiner:**
 
 
• Dobereiner introduced the concept of **triads** in **1829**, grouping three elements with similar properties where the middle element had properties that were an average of the other two.
 
• This concept was an early step towards understanding periodicity but was limited in scope.
 
 
 
• **Lothar Meyer:**
 
 
• Meyer independently developed a periodic table around the same time as Mendeleev but did not receive the same recognition as his table was less comprehensive.
 
• He plotted atomic volume against atomic mass to show periodic trends but did not predict undiscovered elements as Mendeleev did.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The **Periodic Table** organizes elements based on increasing atomic number and recurring chemical properties.
 
• Modern periodic tables are based on the work of Mendeleev but use atomic numbers instead of atomic masses.
 
• The table is divided into groups and periods, with elements sharing similar properties placed in the same column.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mendeleev's prediction:**

 
 
• He predicted the existence and properties of several elements like **eka-aluminum** (later discovered as gallium) and **eka-silicon** (later discovered as germanium).
 
• This ability to predict elements made his periodic table more widely accepted compared to other models.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Trends:**
 
 
• Key periodic trends include **atomic radius, electronegativity, ionization energy, and electron affinity**, which are crucial in understanding chemical properties.
 
 
 
• **Modern Periodic Table:**
 
 
• The modern periodic table, based on the **Moseley’s periodic law**, arranges elements by their atomic number instead of atomic mass.
 
• It includes **18 groups** and **7 periods**, accommodating over **118 elements** discovered so far.

⇒ According to the BODMAS rule, perform the division operation first:

⇒ (−60) ÷ (−10) = 6

⇒ Substitute this value back into the expression:

⇒ (−9) − 6 + (−4) × 7

⇒ −9 − 6 − 28

questions.question: The product of the LCM and HCF of two numbers is 150. The difference of the two numbers is 5. Find the numbers.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF = 150.

Given difference between the numbers = 5.

Check the given pairs to find which numbers give a product of 150 and a difference of 5.

The pair 15 and 10 satisfies both conditions (15 × 10 = 150 and 15 − 10 = 5).

**∴ The correct answer is 15, 10.**

**Given:**

Product of LCM and HCF = 150

Difference of the two numbers = 5

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

**Calculation:**

Let the smaller number be y and the larger number be x.

⇒ x − y = 5

⇒ x = y + 5

⇒ x × y = 150

⇒ (y + 5) × y = 150

⇒ y² + 5y − 150 = 0

⇒ y² + 15y − 10y − 150 = 0

⇒ y(y + 15) − 10(y + 15) = 0

⇒ (y − 10)(y + 15) = 0

⇒ The roots are y = 10 and y = −15.

⇒ Since numbers are assumed to be positive in this context, y = 10.

⇒ x = 10 + 5 = 15

**∴ The correct answer is 15, 10.**

Product Rule of LCM and HCF

The product of two given numbers is exactly equal to the product of their HCF and LCM. Formula: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B). Note that this rule applies only to two numbers, not for three or more.

Co-Prime Numbers

If two numbers are co-prime (having no common factor other than 1), their HCF is exactly 1, and their LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.

HCF and LCM of Fractions

HCF of fractions = (HCF of Numerators) ÷ (LCM of Denominators). LCM of fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators).

Time saved by Anmol = 6 hours (late initially) + 2 hours (early now) = 8 hours.

questions.question: The sum of the squares of two consecutive even natural numbers is 2740. The sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the average of the two consecutive even numbers be 'a' (which will be an odd number).

The numbers can be written as (a − 1) and (a + 1), and their required sum is simply 2a.

Sum of their squares = (a − 1)² + (a + 1)² = 2740

⇒ 2(a² + 1) = 2740 ⇒ a² + 1 = 1370 ⇒ a² = 1369 ⇒ a = 37

The sum of the numbers = 2 × 37 = 74.

**∴ The correct answer is 74.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The sum of the squares of two consecutive even natural numbers is 2740.

**Method Used:**

Use the algebraic identity: (x + y)² = x² + 2xy + y²

**Calculations:**

Let the two consecutive even natural numbers be x and x + 2.

⇒ x² + (x + 2)² = 2740

⇒ x² + x² + 4x + 4 = 2740

⇒ 2x² + 4x − 2736 = 0

Dividing the entire equation by 2, we get:

⇒ x² + 2x − 1368 = 0

Now, split the middle term to factorize the quadratic equation:

⇒ x² + 38x − 36x − 1368 = 0

⇒ x(x + 38) − 36(x + 38) = 0

⇒ (x − 36)(x + 38) = 0

Since natural numbers cannot be negative, x cannot be −38. Therefore, x = 36.

The two consecutive even numbers are 36 and 38.

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 36 + 38 = 74

**∴ The correct answer is 74.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula: S = n(n + 1) ÷ 2.

Sum of Squares of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the squares of the first n natural numbers is calculated using: S = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) ÷ 6.

Properties of Even Numbers

The sum or difference of any two even numbers is always even. The square of any even number is always a multiple of 4.

Quadratic Roots Formula

For a standard quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0, the roots can be directly found using: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.
</p
